documents.title: Corbus Pharmaceuticals Reports Results from Phase 1a Study of Oral CB1 Inverse Agonist CRB-913 for the Treatment for Obesity Demonstrating Favorable Safety Profile and Emerging Evidence of Weight Loss
documents.text: Corbus reported results from a double-blinded placebo-controlled single ascending dose and multiple ascending dose Phase 1a study of CRB-913, conducted in the United States, assessing safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of escalating once-daily doses. The single ascending dose portion of the study enrolled 64 participants across 8 cohorts receiving ascending doses of CRB-913 up to a maximal dose of 600 mg per day, or placebo, dosed orally once. The company's headline describes a favorable safety profile and emerging evidence of weight loss.

documents.title: Corbus Pharmaceuticals Announces Last Patient Last Visit in CANYON-1 Study of CRB-913 for the Treatment of Obesity
documents.text: Corbus announced last patient last visit in the CANYON-1 study of CRB-913 for the treatment of obesity. CANYON-1 is a Phase 1b, 16-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study in 240 obese, non-diabetic participants, with a placebo cohort and three CRB-913 cohorts at 20 mg, 40 mg and 60 mg dosed orally once daily. The study is on track for a topline data readout in September 2026.

documents.title: CB1 class history and CRB-913 brain penetration versus monlunabant
documents.text: The first generation of experimental drugs in the CB1 class was abandoned because of potential neuropsychiatric adverse event risks. CRB-913 is described as a highly peripherally restricted oral small molecule CB1 inverse agonist, and yielded 15 times lower brain penetration than monlunabant in mice. CANYON-1 is expected to provide clarifying insights as to its safety and efficacy and to allow contextualisation of the data in comparison to both oral GLP-1 agonists and the CB1 inverse agonist monlunabant.

documents.title: Corbus pipeline: CRB-701 and CRB-913
documents.text: The Corbus pipeline includes CRB-701, a next-generation antibody drug conjugate for the treatment of Nectin-4-expressing tumors, and CRB-913, an orally delivered highly peripherally restricted CB1 inverse agonist for the treatment of obesity.
